Time-varying parameter VAR with stochastic volatility

Source: R/tvp.R
tvpvar.Rd

Bayesian TVP-VAR of Cogley & Sargent (2001, 2005) and Primiceri (2005), with the Gibbs-sampler ordering of Del Negro & Primiceri (2015): $$y_t = X_t'B_t + u_t,\quad u_t = A_t^{-1}\Lambda_t^{1/2}\varepsilon_t,\quad \varepsilon_t\sim N(0,I_K),$$ $$\beta_t=\mathrm{vec}(B_t)=\beta_{t-1}+\eta_t,\ \eta_t\sim N(0,Q);\quad \alpha_t=\alpha_{t-1}+\zeta_t,\ \zeta_t\sim N(0,S);\quad \log\lambda_{it}=\log\lambda_{i,t-1}+\nu_{it},\ \nu_{it}\sim N(0,W_i),$$ where \(X_t=(1,y_{t-1}',\dots,y_{t-p}')'\), \(A_t\) is unit lower triangular with free elements \(\alpha_t\), \(\Sigma_t=A_t^{-1}\Lambda_tA_t^{-1\prime}\) and \(S\) is block diagonal with one block per row of \(A_t\). Each Gibbs sweep draws, in order, \(\beta^T|A^T,\Lambda^T,Q\), \(\alpha^T|\beta^T,\Lambda^T,S\), the Kim-Shephard-Chib (Omori et al. 2007, 10-component) mixture indicators and \(\log\lambda^T|\beta^T,\alpha^T,W\), and finally \(Q,S,W\) from their (inverse-) Wishart / gamma conditionals. State paths are drawn with the Durbin-Koopman (2002) simulation smoother (cost linear in \(T\), quadratic in the state dimension), all in C++ with R's RNG.

Usage

tvpvar(
  Y,
  p = 2L,
  ndraw = 5000L,
  nburn = 2000L,
  thin = 1L,
  const = TRUE,
  sv = TRUE,
  tv_beta = TRUE,
  tv_A = TRUE,
  q_diag = FALSE,
  prior = tvp_prior(),
  nsave_paths = min(ndraw, 1000L),
  reject_explosive = FALSE,
  max_tries = 10L,
  vars = NULL
)

Arguments

Y

data frame (preferred), ts or numeric matrix (T x K) of endogenous variables. Non-numeric columns of a data frame are dropped; a Date column is kept as $dates and used by the plots.

p

lag order.

ndraw

number of retained draws.

nburn

burn-in iterations.

thin

keep every thin-th sweep.

const

include a constant.

sv

stochastic volatility (TRUE) or constant diagonal \(\Lambda\) (FALSE).

tv_beta, tv_A

time-varying coefficients / contemporaneous matrix \(A_t\).

q_diag

diagonal \(Q\) (independent inverse-gamma priors) instead of a full inverse-Wishart.

prior

a tvp_prior().

nsave_paths

number of (evenly spaced) retained draws for which the complete state paths are stored (memory is nsave_paths x T x K(Kp+1) doubles); impulse responses, volatilities and forecasts are computed from these. Posterior means of the paths use all draws.

reject_explosive

redraw the coefficient path (up to max_tries times, otherwise keep the previous path) when any date has a companion root outside the unit circle.

max_tries

see reject_explosive.

vars

<tidy-select> endogenous variables (default: all numeric columns). A Date column of a data frame supplies the dates of the paths.

Value

a `tvpvar` object. Methods: [print()], [summary()], [coef()], [irf()] (`date=`), [fevd()], [forecast()], [tidy()][tidy.tvpvar()], [autoplot()][autoplot.tvpvar()], plus [irf_path()] and [tvp_volatility()].

Details

Special cases: tv_A = FALSE gives the Cogley-Sargent (2005) model (time-varying coefficients and volatilities, constant contemporaneous matrix); sv = FALSE, tv_A = FALSE is the Cogley-Sargent (2001) model with homoskedastic innovations; tv_beta = FALSE freezes the coefficients (a Bayesian VAR with SV, the benchmark for judging whether time variation is needed). The recursive ordering of the variables matters whenever tv_A or sv is on, because \(A_t\) imposes a Cholesky structure on \(\Sigma_t\).

Economic intuition. Time variation in \(B_t\) is a changing transmission mechanism (for example a monetary policy rule that responds more strongly to inflation after Volcker); time variation in \(\Lambda_t\) is a change in the size of shocks (the Great Moderation, the 2008 and 2020 episodes); time variation in \(A_t\) is a change in the contemporaneous propagation of shocks. These are conceptually distinct, and a model that omits stochastic volatility will tend to push heteroskedasticity into the coefficients. Pitfalls: (i) the prior on Q (see tvp_prior()) is informative and drives how much coefficient variation is found; (ii) with many lags the state dimension (\(K(Kp+1)\)) is large relative to the sample, so keep p small; (iii) the first tau observations are used up as a training sample and are not part of the estimation sample; (iv) draws of \(B_t\) may be explosive at some dates: use reject_explosive = TRUE for the (slow) Cogley-Sargent stability truncation.

References

Cogley & Sargent (2005), Primiceri (2005), Del Negro & Primiceri (2015), Durbin & Koopman (2002).

See also

Other TVP-VAR: irf_path(), tidy.tvpvar(), tvp_dynamics, tvp_prior(), tvp_volatility()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- tvpvar(yraw, p = 2, ndraw = 500, nburn = 500)
fit
#> <tvpvar> TVP-VAR(2), K = 3, estimation sample T = 173 (43 - 215), training tau = 40
#>   coefficients: time-varying; A_t: time-varying; volatility: stochastic
#>   500 retained draws, 500 stored paths
autoplot(fit, "vol")

autoplot(fit, "irf", shock = rate, response = infl, horizon = c(0, 4, 8))

plot(irf(fit, date = 50, horizon = 12))

# }
